pr_body:
Previously the docs were very minimalistic. The most important thing missing from the docs
was that people should primarily use higher level APIs instead of using ROUTES directly.

It would be nice to holistically overhaul more of the router API docs, but that's out of
scope of this change.

Fixes #39350

# 📚 Docs or angular.io bug report

### Description

<!-- ✍️edit:--> A clear and concise description of the problem...
Injection token `ROUTES` is sometimes needed in applications where router configuration is fetched dynamically. Providing `ROUTES` allows that to work. As of the moment, documentations relating to dynamic routing or just the `ROUTES` injection token is close to non-existing. `ROUTES` does have https://angular.io/api/router/ROUTES but it's essentially empty.

## 🔬 Minimal Reproduction

### What's the affected URL?**
<!-- ✍️edit:--> https://angular.io/...
https://angular.io/api/router/ROUTES


### Expected vs Actual Behavior**
<!-- If applicable please describe the difference between the expected and actual behavior after following the repro steps. -->
<!-- ✍️edit:-->
Documentations for `ROUTES` need to be filled with more information.
comments:
@AndrewKushnir @IgorMinar
The URL was accidentally renamed to https://angular.io/api/router/ROUTES-1.

@LayZeeDK - the rename of the path for ROUTES was not accidental - it was to account for the ambiguity on case-insensitive file-systems of the `ROUTES` and `Routes` API pages. There is now a disambiguation page at `https://angular.io/api/router/routes`. But @IgorMinar has suggested a better approach that does not require these URL changes, which I will implement today.
@petebacondarwin Thanks for explaining. I see the problem.

review_comments: Is it worth saying something like "Some complex use-cases may require providing the routes with a `FactoryProvider`"? I agree that we shouldn't try to provide examples of these complex scenarios because they're abundant and application-specific but it be useful to at least acknowledge that we understand there are times it is actually necessary (e.g. [router_module_wrapper](http://cs/google3/cloud/console/web/common/router_module_wrapper/router_module_wrapper.ts)).

That seems like such an advanced use case that mentioning it here just confuses the 99% of readers. I think we should skip it as most of these experts already know how they can provision this injectable in fancy ways.
